system:
You are checking a claim about a statutory provision. Refute it if it can be refuted, but ONLY on the two grounds set out below. Do not invent stricter grounds.

WHAT THE CLAIM MEANS. It asserts the provision makes one quantity bear on another in one of these specific ways. Judge it against the relation actually claimed:
  gate          - makes the second available or unavailable by reference to the first, e.g. a threshold.
  formula_input - the first enters a calculation of the second.
  limit         - the first caps or floors the second. A provision that disregards earnings above a maximum DOES limit an earnings-based award: that is a sound limit claim, not a failed determination claim.
  adjustment    - the first discounts or increases the second. A contributory negligence provision DOES adjust damages by reference to fault: that is a sound adjustment claim.

TWO THINGS THAT ARE NOT GROUNDS FOR REFUSAL.
  1. The provision does not use the variable's name. It never will -- legislation does not use dataset column names, and requiring it would refute every true claim. 'Net weekly earnings' IS pre-accident weekly income. 'Contributory negligence' IS about clarity of fault. 'Degree of permanent impairment' IS whole person impairment. Conceptual correspondence is required of you, not optional.
  2. The relationship is indirect, partial, conditional, or shared with other factors. Almost every statutory rule is. Only the claimed relation has to hold.

THE TWO REAL GROUNDS FOR REFUSAL.
  (a) SUBJECT MISMATCH. The provision governs a different quantity from the one the claim says it bears on. A provision about an insurer's duty to PAY FOR treatment does not govern HOW MUCH TREATMENT the claimant underwent. A provision conferring jurisdiction to assess a claim does not make one assessed quantity determine another.
  (b) WORD MATCHING. The claim followed a word rather than a meaning -- reading 'injury caused by the fault of the driver' (a fault condition) as being about how DIFFICULT causation is to establish.

Refuse on (a) or (b). Otherwise the claim stands.

PROVISION: 95 Motor Accidents Compensation Act 1999

--- BEGIN PROVISION TEXT ---
95
 
Status of assessments
(1)
 An assessment under this Part of the issue of liability for a claim is not binding on any party to the assessment.
(2)
 An assessment under this Part of the amount of damages for liability under a claim is binding on the insurer, and the insurer must pay to the claimant the amount of damages specified in the certificate as to the assessment if—
(a)
 the insurer accepts that liability under the claim, and
(b)
 the claimant accepts that amount of damages in settlement of the claim within 21 days after the certificate of assessment is issued.
Note.
If the amount of damages is not accepted by the claimant within that period, section 151 makes provision with respect to liability for legal costs incurred after the certificate of assessment was issued.
(2A)
 The amount of damages payable by an insurer (including any costs assessed as payable by the insurer) must be paid within such period as may be prescribed by the regulations and the regulations may require the payment of interest on so much of the amount payable as is from time to time unpaid after the end of that period. The rate of interest may be set by reference to the rate of interest prescribed for the purposes of section 101 of the 
Civil Procedure Act 2005
 but may not exceed that rate.
(3)
 It is a condition of an insurer’s licence under Part 7.1 that the insurer complies with this section.
s 95:
 Am 2007 No 95, Sch 1 [61].
--- END PROVISION TEXT ---

THE CLAIM: this provision makes 'Liability Clarity' (an ordinal score for how clear fault is) bear on 'Lump Sum' (the total dollar amount awarded to the claimant), as a gate.
Quoted in support: "An assessment under this Part of the issue of liability for a claim is not binding on any party to the assessment."
Mapping offered: The concept of 'liability under the claim' relates to how clear fault is, which corresponds to 'Liability Clarity'.

Refute this claim if it can be refuted.

response.objection: The provision does not make 'Liability Clarity' a gate for 'Lump Sum'; it only states that liability assessments are non-binding, which does not control access to the lump sum award.
